chunks: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, as provision for you and for the travelers.”
Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “It is its salted food which you eat.”

And he said: “The distinction between the two is that every bird that is in the reed-beds, lays eggs on land, and hatches on land, then it is land game. And whatever bird is on land, but lays eggs in the sea and hatches in the sea, then it is from sea game.”

key_terms.الْآجَامِ: reed-beds or marsh thickets where certain birds may dwell
key_terms.صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ: game caught from the sea, treated as lawful in the cited verse
key_terms.صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ: land game, identified by where the bird lays and hatches
key_terms.طَعَامُهُ: the food of the sea, explained here as its salted edible produce
key_terms.مَلِيحُهُ: its salted food, interpreted as what people eat from the sea
key_terms.يُفْرِخُ: hatches or brings forth its young

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام distinguish between land game and sea game in the verse about the game of the sea?
ai.summary: This hadith cites the Qur'anic ruling that sea game and its food are lawful, then explains part of the verse through the statement of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام. It also gives a juridical distinction between land game and sea game based on where birds lay eggs and hatch their young.
